chapter: Postwar: Chicago, Vinson, Hines and Cootie
title: Session work in New York: Billie Holiday and the Ink Spots
summary: While with Vinson he played dates with Billie Holiday, Roy Eldridge and the Ink Spots, arranged through Mo Gale.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: So then, the next sessions were with Cleanhead, I guess, huh?
Well, maybe with Cleanhead. No, I could have been with Cleanhead. No, no, I was doing record dates with other groups around New York.
While you were working with Cleanhead?
Oh, sure, yeah.
Were you? Well, try to remember who you were recording with.
I was even trying to remember this band leader I asked you about a few minutes ago.
Yeah, we should have asked your wife.
And I even made some records with Billie Holiday.
Did you? And with Teddy, you mean?
No, Teddy wasn't on this. She had the other piano player, that did a lot of arrangements.
Sonny.
Sonny who?
White. That was -- no, he came later, didn't he?
No, he came later. This was -- maybe I'll find it in the book here.
Yeah. Well, never mind. I don't remember who Billie was using then.
Because Roy Eldridge was on the date, too.
He was?
Oh, yeah, he made a lot of things dates with her.
Yeah, I know he did. Chu Choo -- well, Roy
Chu and Choo made a --
Well, this was a small group, yeah.
Yeah.
Choo and Roy, they did a lot of things
Yeah. Were you on those sessions with them?
No, not with Chu, not with Chu, no.
No.
And also, the Inkspots. I made some records with them.
You did? Well, that's because of Mo Gale.
Well, yes.
Because Gale was handling them.
Sure.
How about that? So you didn't go into New York like a newcomer at all, did you? You fell right in, huh?
Well, I feel right in, I guess because --
Of course, one thing is good. There weren't that many good drummers.
Oh, they had some good drummers there, but --
